title: Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces
displayName: Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces

statements.hypotheses: S smooth integral projective over C, L ample; r >= r0(S,L); outside a countable union of proper closed subsets in ordered distinct configurations Ur.
conclusions: Boundary divisor pi*L-sqrt(L^2/r) sum Ei is nef
statements.checking: Statement, all conclusions and proof p.17 read.

statements.hypotheses: For every k,m>0 with m>k sqrt(H/r), no nonzero section of kL vanishes to order at least m at all fixed distinct points.
conclusions: The boundary divisor is nef, hence tests all integral curves including unequal multiplicities.
statements.checking: Full statement and contradiction argument read.

statements.hypotheses: K uncountable algebraically closed of characteristic zero; smooth integral projective surface and ample line bundle.
conclusions: For all sufficiently large r, equality outside a countable union of proper closed subsets, with nonempty complement.
statements.checking: Full statement and descent/base-change proof read.

proofPassages.scope: Finite minors, distinct initial monomial basis, weighted analytic rescaling and convergence.
Nodal divisor, removal of components, intersection bound, slice compression, transfer to the surface.
Triangle multiplicity estimate, character projection, index-r lattice, primitive direction for all large r, quantifier order.

proofPassages.results: Lemmas 5.1–5.2, Proposition 5.3, Lemma 5.4, Theorem 1.1 proof, Corollary 5.5
proofPassages.scope: Open locus, very general complement, RR effective divisor, upper bound, field extension.
